clue.text: One could be across or down

definitions.text: One could be across or down

parts.words: One could be across or down
parts.note: the solver reads this as crossword talk about a clue's direction, but 'across' and 'down' are also words like 'over' and 'under' that show position

explanation.surface: It sounds like a remark about where an entry sits in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The crossword setting pushes you to think of grid entries, but the clue is really about grammar: 'across' and 'down' both belong to one class of word.
explanation.definitionFit: Across and down are both examples of the part of speech that relates a noun to its position or direction.

clue.text: Monarchy accepting one's fidelity

indicators.note: a word that takes something in holds it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a monarchy is a kingdom, or realm
one is I, and 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A kingdom welcoming a subject's loyalty to the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: In art, faithful reproduction of life as it is: truthfulness to nature is called fidelity.

clue.text: Massive 'Queen Elizabeth' in Atlantic over by America

parts.note: the Atlantic Ocean is jokingly called the pond
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
US stands for the United States

explanation.surface: The liner Queen Elizabeth, enormous, crossing the Atlantic towards America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Elizabeth' looks like the ocean liner, but it gives only ER, the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heavy and bulky in its weight is ponderous, a synonym of massive.

clue.text: Has around million oil wells

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, holding it inside

parts.note: to have a drink or meal is to sup, so has is sups

explanation.surface: Someone owns about a million oil wells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' looks like ownership, but it means eats or drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is the reservoir at the bottom of an engine where lubricating oil collects.

clue.text: Capital charged following case of terrible explosive

a case is the outside of something, so the first and last letters of the next word are taken

to charge is to run or rush, so charged is ran

explanation.surface: A city was attacked after a terrible bomb went off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests an accusation or an electric charge, but it means rushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Teheran, more often written Tehran, is the chief city and seat of government of Iran.

clue.text: Head holding sanctimonious view

indicators.note: one piece grips the other, which sits inside it

parts.note: onion is old slang for the head
pi is a short form of pious, meaning sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A leader stubbornly keeps a self-righteous outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a leader, but it is the slang word for the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view, the way a person sees a matter.

clue.text: With small cane, raise one's hat, initially aloof

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat or cane them
to doff is to raise or take off one's hat
one is I, and 's stands for is

indicators.note: only the start of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A haughty gentleman with his walking stick lifting his hat in greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cane' looks like a walking stick in this picture, but it means to beat, as tanning a hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standoffish keeps people at a distance, which is what being aloof means.

clue.text: Feel shame for author, almost, penning 'Hotel'

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the next piece is held inside
the word is not quite complete: its final letter goes

parts.note: an author is a writer
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A writer feels embarrassed while writing about a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' keeps the writing picture going, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirm or twist in embarrassment is to writhe, as one does when feeling acute shame.

clue.text: About time to return, come down making land

indicators.note: returning goes back, so the letters of about and time are read in the opposite order

parts.note: re means about or concerning
rain comes down from the sky

explanation.surface: Nearly time to come back and descend: a pilot preparing to land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a verb, the end of the descent, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land considered by its physical features.

clue.text: Express after instant hard material

indicators.note: the express piece is placed after the other two

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to air a view is to express it

explanation.surface: A rushed delivery of tough fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' and 'instant' both suggest speed, but they are separate pieces: air and moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is a fabric or yarn woven from the hair of the Angora goat.

clue.text: Queen, always Queen, in hit English boom

parts.note: R is short for Regina, queen
ever means always

indicators.note: the second queen goes inside the word for hit

parts.note: to bat is to hit
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A tribute to the Queen echoing through an English hit record.
explanation.definitionFit: To boom is to resound loudly, the sound echoing as it does when it reverberates.

clue.text: Compound net interest starts with stock

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the two words before are used

parts.note: a stock phrase is a trite one

explanation.surface: A finance lesson: compound and net interest, starting with stocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' sits with 'interest' in a finance picture, but it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrite is a salt or ester of nitrous acid, a chemical compound.

clue.text: Fancy girl? Finish off in stable

indicators.note: the shortened girl goes inside the stable word

parts.note: something sure is steady or stable

indicators.note: the end of the word is taken away

parts.note: a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A pretty girl? Finishing the day in the stables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like a horses' home, but it is the adjective meaning firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to imagine or suppose it, which is what to surmise means.

clue.text: Greek character with turn after poem in theatre

indicators.note: the Greek letter comes after the poem

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek actor performs a twist after reciting a poem on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeum was a roofed building in ancient Greece or Rome for musical performances, a kind of theatre.

clue.text: Love flowed around row before church ceremony

indicators.note: these pieces go ahead of the church

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the word for flowed goes around the row word

parts.note: to run is to flow, so flowed is ran
din is a noisy row
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Affection overflowed around the quarrel before a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a line, but it is a noisy argument.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance can be a religious rite or prescribed ritual, such as communion.

clue.text: Most boring ass that is taking Duke to the front

indicators.note: the duke letter is picked up and carried
the letter carried is set down at the start

parts.note: rear is a word for the backside, an ass
id est is the Latin for that is, shortened to i.e.

explanation.surface: The dullest donkey is the one carrying a duke on its front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ass' looks like the donkey, but it is the backside. Joining the backside word to the Latin gives REARIDEST; 'taking ... to the front' moves its D to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreariest is the superlative of dreary, so it means dullest or most tedious.

clue.text: Fill turnover in speciality appetiser

indicators.note: the reversed fill sits inside the speciality

parts.note: a forte is a person's strong point, their speciality

indicators.note: turned over, the letters for fill read backwards

parts.note: to sate is to fill to satisfaction

explanation.surface: A baker fills a turnover pastry as their signature starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like the pastry, but it signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetiser gives a small taste of what is to come, a sample before the main experience.

clue.text: Beam excellent? This compiler's put away!

parts.note: rad is slang for excellent
the compiler speaks of themself as I
to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: The setter Beam asks if they are excellent, then announces their dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: Beam is the setter's own pseudonym, so the clue opens on the setter's name; 'This compiler's put away' reads as I have eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to shine or send out rays of light, which is what to radiate means.

clue.text: Cachalot's end with going-over prepared for blubber

indicators.note: only the last letter of the whale's name is used

parts.note: an earful is a scolding, a going-over

explanation.surface: A whale's demise as whalers process it for its fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' looks like whale fat, as the cachalot (sperm whale) suggests, but it means to cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tearful is close to weeping, ready to blubber, which is to sob noisily.

clue.text: Sound of record turning, naff first to last

indicators.note: the record letters are read the other way round

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: the first letter of the word moves to its end

parts.note: naff and bum are both British slang for poor or rubbish

explanation.surface: The noise of a spinning record, a bad one that came last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like noise, but it is the verb meaning to measure depth.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb the depths is to sound them, measuring water depth with a weighted line.

clue.text: Mercurial memory held by Greek god

indicators.note: one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
learning by rote is learning from memory

explanation.surface: A Greek god keeps a fickle memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mercurial' brings to mind Mercury, the Roman god, but the god here is Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Protean, after the shape-changing sea god Proteus, describes something changeable, as mercurial does.

clue.text: Married and separated with change of heart

indicators.note: the middle two letters of the word are changed round

parts.note: things untied have been loosened and separated

explanation.surface: A couple who married, split, then had a change of heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A married couple are joined together, wed in a union.

clue.text: Weapon sky-high in failure almost returned

the shortened failure word is read backwards
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a miss is a failure
sky-high prices are dear

explanation.surface: A missile soaring sky-high fails and nearly comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MISS to MIS, and 'returned' turns that into SIM, which takes in DEAR.

clue.text: Lover embracing the Italian football team

clue.text: Bold paw grabbing top of nude female

clue.text: Most tranquil river leaves mountain for north

parts.note: Everest is the world's highest mountain

explanation.definitionFit: Evenest is the superlative of even, in its sense of calm and placid, so most tranquil.

clue.text: Rubber protection for members?

parts.note: the members here are legs, and the protection is rubber boots that come up to the knee

explanation.surface: A sly hint at condoms for, say, club members.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at something saucier, but the members are legs and the rubber is boots; Britons call such boots after the Duke who popularised them.
explanation.definitionFit: These knee-high waterproof rubber boots cover and protect the lower legs.
